text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - UK shares ended a volatile session sharply lower as Wall Street plunged during London trading hours on fears that U.S. blue chips may be overpriced and due for a correction, dealers and strategists said. The FTSE 100 index dropped 53.2 points or 1.3 percent to close at 3,982.5.

FRANKFURT - German shares end bourse dealings lower as the dollar neared its lowest level for over a week and with nervousness creeping back about the U.S. market after a fall in the S&P futures contract. The 30-share DAX index closed down 49.95 points at 2,841.05. In post-bourse trade the index fell 54.59 to 2,836.36.

PARIS - French shares suffered heavy losses at the close, unsettled by Wall Street's drop. Paris had been retracing some of its sharp retreat as it looked as the Dow was steadying but by the close, New York was still under pressure as U.S. treasuries weakened. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 38.12 points or 1.69 percent at 2,213.28.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended lower but above the day's lows while chemicals group Clariant surged more than 12 percent, extending yesterday's strong gain. U.S. PPI data sent mixed signals and did not influence prices much, dealers said. Swiss indices moved off the day's low after Wall Street's early losses proved only moderate. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 16.89 points, or 0.68 percent, at 2,464.85.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended sharply lower on Wednesday with most of the market preoccupied with the debut of Tokyo Disneyland operator Oriental Land Co Ltd. Futures-linked sales especially helped drag the benchmark down in the afternoon session. The Nikkei 225 closed 253.74 points or 1.22 percent lower at 20,568.38.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks reversed course on Wednesday afternoon to close sharply down, due to inflation and currency worries and negative trends in local and overseas futures markets. The Hang Seng Index fell 152.86 points to close at 13,189.60.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed slightly weaker on Wednesday, the market shrugging off early strength inspired by a surprise rate cut and focusing on the effect of a strong local currency on the resource sector and possible Wall Street weakness. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 2.5 points weaker at 2,359.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African near-term industrial futures took a whack at the start of trade on Wednesday and struggled to regain composure throughout the day, dragging industrial shares down with them. The industrial index was 45.6 points off at 7,851.8, the all-shares lost 27.3 points to 6,639.1 and the golds inched up 15.4 points to 1,542.1.
